mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a financial crisis.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for three consecutive months indicates an overheating labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of triggered periods, or the effect is absent during periods of high inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A double-digit year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals a sharp contraction in household demand, which reduces revenue for consumer-facing firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not observed during a supply-side shock.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and capital expenditure, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 65% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during a tech-driven expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 5-year averages signals a monetary policy tightening coinciding with accelerating inflation, which increases real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a deflationary shock.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the civilian labor force participation rate (implied by PAYEMS and UNRATE) by more than 0.4 percentage points in one month, combined with a concurrent rise in unemployment, signals a loosening labor market with increased slack, which supports monetary easing and boosts equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises AND (PAYEMS growth > 0.4% in one month)
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during a wage-price spiral.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves negative 60-day returns in more than 65% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not present during a broader economic downturn.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained quarterly decline in real GDP (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals an economic recession, which reduces corporate earnings and increases default risk, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during a synchronized global recovery.
